strings.name: Dina Katabi
strings.summary: Dina Katabi studies wireless networks, machine learning and digital health. She is MIT’s Thuan and Nicole Pham Professor and directs its Center for Wireless Networks and Mobile Computing. With collaborators, she uses reflected radio signals to study contactless measurement of movement, breathing and sleep, alongside communication interference and data transmission. She co-founded Emerald Innovations to translate health-monitoring technology. These studies concern measurement and disease assessment, not treatments or universally applicable clinical conclusions.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth is given only as 1971. Sources differ on her master’s year and company founding year, so neither is specified. The 2017 ACM prize is distinguished from its 2018 announcement, and 2026 reporting from the earlier selection.
strings.influence.rationale: Advances wireless sensing, networking and digital-health research, exploring contactless human monitoring using wireless signals.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a Damascus University bachelor’s in 1995, followed by an MIT master’s and a doctorate in 2003.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research focus
strings.facts.f2.value: Wireless communication, machine learning and contactless health monitoring; devices use radio reflections, not X-rays.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Wireless networking research
strings.highlights.h1.text: Works with collaborators on interference, congestion and signal processing to improve transmission efficiency and reliability.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Contactless health sensing
strings.highlights.h2.text: Studies movement, breathing and sleep with radio signals and machine learning, exploring Parkinson’s assessment with clinical collaborators.
strings.timeline.t1.title: MIT reviews 2026 honors
strings.timeline.t1.text: MIT’s summer-honors roundup confirms her inclusion in Forbes and Know Your Value’s 2026 50 Over 50 list; this is the report date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Elected to National Academy of Medicine
strings.timeline.t2.text: NAM announces her election, recognizing contactless health monitoring and digital-biomarker research.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Nocturnal-breathing study published
strings.timeline.t3.text: The team publishes Parkinson’s assessment research in Nature Medicine, with Yuzhe Yang as first author and Katabi as senior author; it is not a treatment trial.
strings.timeline.t4.title: MIT announces named professorship
strings.timeline.t4.text: MIT names her the inaugural Thuan and Nicole Pham Professor, recognizing research and student mentoring.
strings.timeline.t5.title: ACM Prize announcement
strings.timeline.t5.text: Wins the 2017 ACM Prize in Computing for wireless-system contributions; the announcement appears in 2018.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Receives MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.t6.text: The foundation announces her inclusion in its 2013 class for wireless-network and data-exchange research.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completes doctorate and joins MIT faculty
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earns her MIT doctorate and joins its faculty in the same year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns Damascus University bachelor’s
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes undergraduate electrical engineering before pursuing further study at MIT.
